documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.body:
Front desk: Pt called to establish care, moved from the Bronx in August, turned 18 last month so can't stay with his pediatrician. Requests Spanish-speaking provider. Says he takes a daily anxiety medicine and has about 5 pills left; NY pediatric office won't send more since he's out of state. Routed to RN.

RN: Spoke with pt in Spanish. Anxiety med 50 mg daily x ~1.5 yrs (name not on hand, will bring bottle), no missed doses so far. Denies SI, no thoughts of self-harm. Feels 'ok, a little stressed with the move.' Moved new-patient appt up to 12/9 with PCP (cancellation slot). Advised to bring pill bottle and any vaccine card. Release form for pediatric records emailed to him. Pt agreeable.

conditions.note: Diagnosed by prior pediatrician; on sertraline

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily as needed in spring

documents.title: New Patient — Establish Care
documents.body:
Visit conducted in Spanish (pt's preference; conversational English).

CC: establish care, needs sertraline.

HPI: 18M, moved from the Bronx Aug 2024 with mother and sister, living with aunt in Southampton. Anxiety since ~spring 2023 (10th grade): constant worry about school and family, trouble falling asleep, stomach knots, a few episodes of racing heart and shaky hands before exams. Pediatrician diagnosed GAD, started sertraline 25 mg, increased to 50 mg spring 2024 'because it wasn't doing enough.' Saw school counselor in the Bronx; no therapy since moving. Says sertraline helps 'some' -- worry is less constant, but the move, new job and money stress have made the last 2 months harder. No panic attacks since summer. Had an as-needed pill for anxiety in 2023, stopped -- 'me dejaba dormido.' Denies SI/HI, no self-harm history, no psychiatric hospitalizations.

PMH: GAD. Seasonal allergies (cetirizine OTC in spring). No surgeries.
Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily (bottle reviewed; 5 tabs left). Cetirizine 10 mg PRN.
Allergies: amoxicillin -- rash as a small child per mother.
FHx: mother anxiety (treated), hypothyroid. Father HTN. MGM T2DM.
SHx: Full-time PT aide at an outpatient ortho PT clinic in Westfield since Sept; wants to become a physical therapist. Never smoked. Vaped in 10th-11th grade, quit 2023. Alcohol 1-2x/month. Tried cannabis, none now. Gym 4x/week, soccer on weekends. Single. Sleeps 6 h on work nights.

ROS: neg for chest pain, syncope, wt loss. + sleep onset insomnia.

Exam: Well-appearing, slightly fidgety. HEENT nl. Neck no thyromegaly. Heart RRR no murmur (sitting/standing). Lungs clear. Abd benign. Skin: scattered nevi. Mood 'nervous,' affect congruent, linear thought.

PHQ-9 7, GAD-7 14.

A/P:
1. GAD, moderate, partially controlled on sertraline 50. Refilled 50 mg (90 d). Discussed therapy; he wants to try once settled with work schedule -- revisit at follow-up. Sleep hygiene, limit caffeine.
2. Allergic rhinitis -- cetirizine PRN.
3. Health maintenance: flu vaccine today. HIV and hep C screening once, lipid screen (age 17-21) -- labs today. Requested NY pediatric records incl. immunizations.
RTC 6-8 wks (telehealth OK).

documents.title: Screening Labs
documents.body: Lipids normal (LDL 96, HDL 48). HIV and hepatitis C screens nonreactive. No repeat needed unless new risk. Sent to pt via portal in Spanish: 'Sus análisis salieron normales.'

documents.title: Prior Pediatric Records — Bronx
documents.body:
Received by fax from prior pediatric practice in the Bronx, NY (care 2018-2024), 23 pages, after signed release.

Problem list: generalized anxiety disorder (dx 03/2023, PHQ-A/GAD-7 screening at 16-yr well visit, GAD-7 13); seasonal allergic rhinitis.
Medication list (printed 08/2024): sertraline 25 mg daily; hydroxyzine pamoate 25 mg BID PRN anxiety; cetirizine 10 mg daily.
Allergies: amoxicillin (rash, age ~3).
Immunizations: DR vaccine card transcribed 2018 -- hep B x3, DTP series, MMR x2, varicella x2 (dates per card). In NY: Tdap 09/2018; HPV9 09/2018 and 04/2019; COVID-19 mRNA 06/2021 (single dose recorded); MenACWY booster 02/2023. No MenB.
Well visits 2019-2023 unremarkable, growth normal. Note 05/2023: school counselor referral. No ED visits on file.

Note: outside medication list differs from our list (sertraline 50 mg). Routed to clinical pharmacist for reconciliation.

medications.reason: Not taking since 2023; removed at reconciliation

documents.title: Medication Reconciliation
documents.body:
Clinical pharmacist med rec, prompted by outside pediatric records.

Discrepancies (outside list 08/2024 vs ours):
- Sertraline 25 mg (outside) vs 50 mg (ours). Retail pharmacy fill history: sertraline 50 mg #30 filled monthly since 05/2024; 25 mg last filled 04/2024. Called pediatric office -- nurse confirms 50 mg increase was a phone order 05/2024 that never made it onto the printed list. 50 mg is correct.
- Hydroxyzine 25 mg PRN: last fill 09/2023. Called pt (Spanish) -- stopped late 2023, made him too sleepy, no pills at home. Removed from list.
- Cetirizine: OTC, uses only in spring. Kept as PRN.
No interactions of concern. Pt confirms taking sertraline every morning, 0 missed doses this month. List updated.

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up — Anxiety
documents.body:
Video visit, in Spanish. Pt in his car on break at work; identity confirmed, consents to video.

S: Anxiety 'un poco mejor.' Work going well, picking up extra shifts; worries about money and helping his mom with rent. Sleep 6-6.5 h. Drinks 1-2 energy drinks on double-shift days. No panic attacks. Taking sertraline 50 mg daily, no side effects. No SI.

GAD-7 11 (was 14), PHQ-9 6.

A/P: GAD, improving, still moderate symptoms.
- Continue sertraline 50 mg. Discussed going to 100 mg vs adding therapy first; he prefers to try therapy before raising the dose. Reasonable.
- Referral to behavioral health, Spanish-speaking clinician requested, evening/telehealth slots.
- Cut energy drinks to none if possible; at least none after noon.
F/u 2-3 months or sooner PRN.

events.reason: Chest tightness, palpitations, shortness of breath

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 114. PR 142 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 418 ms. Normal axis. No pre-excitation. No ST elevation or depression; no pathologic Q waves. No Brugada pattern. No prior for comparison. Interpreted by ED physician.

documents.title: ED Provider Note
documents.body:
CC: chest tightness, racing heart.

HPI: 18M with GAD on sertraline brought by aunt ~23:15 after sudden onset of chest tightness, pounding heartbeat, feeling he couldn't get a full breath, tingling in both hands and lips, and fear he was 'going to die.' Began ~22:30 at home after a 12-h double shift and an argument on the phone. Had 2 energy drinks and a pre-workout scoop today. Peaked within 10 min, easing by arrival. No exertional component tonight, no syncope, no fever, no recent illness, no leg swelling, no travel, no drugs. Similar but milder episodes before exams in high school.
PMH GAD. Meds sertraline 50 mg. Allergy amoxicillin (rash).

Exam: anxious, tearful, talking in full sentences. HR 118 -> 84 on reassessment. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. No chest wall tenderness. Calves soft, nontender. Perioral tingling resolved with slow breathing coaching.

Data: ECG sinus tach 114, normal intervals, no pre-excitation or Brugada. CBC nl. BMP: glucose 118, K 3.6, otherwise nl. Mg 2.0. hs-TnI 2 and 2 ng/L (0 and 2 h). PERC negative once HR <100.

ED course: lorazepam 0.5 mg PO x1 given 00:20 with good effect; coached breathing. Symptoms resolved.

Impression: panic attack with palpitations and hyperventilation; stimulant/caffeine contribution. ACS, PE, arrhythmia felt unlikely.

Dispo: home with aunt 02:35. No new prescriptions. Stop energy drinks and pre-workout. Follow up with PCP within 1 week. Return for chest pain with exertion, fainting, palpitations that don't stop, or shortness of breath at rest.

documents.title: Post-ED Call
documents.body: RN call after ED notification (3/22-23, panic attack, workup neg). Spoke w/ pt in Spanish. Feels 'cansado pero bien.' One brief episode of heart racing yesterday on couch, ~5 min, settled with breathing. No chest pain now, no fainting. Took sertraline today. Stopped energy drinks. Denies SI. Booked PCP f/u 3/27 at 3:40; pt asks if mom can come -- yes.

conditions.label: Family history of sudden cardiac death
conditions.note: Maternal uncle died suddenly at 34, no autopsy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.body:
In Spanish; mother Ana present with pt's permission.

S: Seen in ED 3/22 for chest tightness, palpitations, hand/lip tingling after double shift + energy drinks; ECG sinus tach, troponins neg x2, labs nl, dx panic attack. Since then 2 more shorter episodes (3/23 at home, 3/26 at work in the supply room), each 5-10 min, out of the blue, heart pounding, 'me voy a morir' feeling. Now worrying about the next one and avoided the gym this week. No more energy drinks.
New info: mother reports her brother died suddenly at 34 in the DR, 'del corazón,' no autopsy; no known pacemakers/ICDs or early heart disease otherwise. Pt does get palpitations during heavy lifting sometimes, no syncope ever.
Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily. No SI.

O: Calm today. HR 88 regular. No murmur supine or with standing/Valsalva. Lungs clear. Thyroid nl.
ED ECG reviewed: no pre-excitation, normal QTc.
GAD-7 13, PHQ-9 8.

A/P:
1. Panic disorder -- recurrent unexpected attacks plus anticipatory worry, on top of GAD. Increase sertraline to 100 mg daily (take 1/2 of new tab x1 wk if GI upset). Reviewed panic physiology, paced breathing, no benzos. BH referral already pending -- messaged BH to flag panic.
2. Palpitations with exertional component + FHx sudden death in young uncle -- low suspicion but warrants cardiology eval (echo/ambulatory monitor) to exclude cardiomyopathy/channelopathy. Referred. Until seen: OK for normal activity and light gym, avoid max lifts/competitive play; stop if chest pain or near-faint.
3. TSH today.
F/u after cardiology or 6 wks.

documents.title: Cardiology Referral
documents.body: Cardiology referral sent: 18M, palpitations incl. with exertion, ED 3/22 sinus tach/neg troponin, maternal uncle sudden death age 34 no autopsy. Q: echo/Holter, screen for HCM/inherited arrhythmia. Interpreter: Spanish. Insurance requires PCP referral on file -- entered. Cardiology scheduling: first available 5/6. Pt notified by phone; put on cancellation list. BH also notified re: panic dx, pt moved up on waitlist.

events.reason: Question about new sertraline dose and exercise

documents.title: sertraline 100 and gym
documents.body: hola doctora, started the 100 on saturday. first 3 days my stomach was bad and kinda nauseous in the morning, now its better. is that normal? also can i go back to the gym or wait for the cardiologist? i miss it lol it helps my stress. no more attacks since last week only felt nervous at work once. gracias

documents.title: RE: sertraline 100 and gym
documents.body:
Hola Josue -- sí, the nausea in the first days of a higher dose is common and usually fades in 1-2 weeks; taking it with breakfast helps. Your thyroid test (TSH) came back normal, so that's not causing the palpitations.
Gym: yes to cardio at a moderate pace and lighter weights where you can still talk. Hold off on max lifts until cardiology sees you on 5/6. If you ever get chest pain, feel faint, or the racing doesn't stop, go to the ED. Glad no more attacks.
-- PCP

documents.title: Behavioral Health Intake
documents.body:
Thank you for referring this 18-year-old for anxiety and new panic attacks. Session conducted in Spanish via telehealth (pt at home, private room).

Presenting concerns: chronic worry since 2023 (school, family finances, immigration-related stress for relatives), now panic attacks since March with an ED visit. Fear of 'another one at work in front of patients.' Has started avoiding the stockroom where one occurred.
History: moved from DR at 11, then Bronx to MA last summer; close to mother and sister; father in DR, limited contact. Feels responsible for helping with rent. Strengths: motivated, works with people all day, clear career goal (PT), supportive aunt.
Risk: denies SI/HI, no history of self-harm, no weapons at home. Protective factors strong. Low risk.
Substances: alcohol rare, no drugs, stopped energy drinks.
GAD-7 12, PHQ-9 7. On sertraline 100 mg (increased 3/27) via PCP.

Impression: GAD with panic disorder; acculturative and financial stressors.
Plan: CBT for panic -- psychoeducation, interoceptive exposure, cognitive restructuring for catastrophic thoughts; graded return to the stockroom. Biweekly telehealth, Tuesdays 5 pm. Coordinate with PCP re: medication.

events.reason: Palpitations; family history of sudden death

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 71. PR 150 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT/QTc 384/416 ms. Normal axis. Early repolarization pattern in V2-V4, within normal limits for a young male. No delta wave, no epsilon wave, no Brugada pattern, no LVH by voltage criteria, no T-wave inversion beyond V1. Compared with ED tracing 3/22/2025: rate slower, otherwise unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Normal sinus rhythm; normal ECG for age.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.body:
Dear Doctor, thank you for asking me to see Mr. Figueroa, an 18-year-old PT aide, for palpitations and a family history of sudden death. Telephone Spanish interpreter used for history.

History: since about March he has had episodes of rapid regular heartbeat, usually with anxiety (ED 3/22: sinus tachycardia 114, hs-troponin negative x2) and occasionally during heavy squats or deadlifts, gradual onset and offset, never with syncope, presyncope or chest pain. Panic episodes now less frequent since sertraline was increased to 100 mg. No energy drinks since March. Maternal uncle died suddenly at 34 in the Dominican Republic, cause unknown, no autopsy; no other family members with sudden death, cardiomyopathy, pacemakers or drowning.

Exam: BP 118/72, HR 74, BMI 23.9. Athletic build. JVP normal. Normal S1 S2, no murmur at rest, with Valsalva or squat-to-stand. Peripheral pulses normal, no radio-femoral delay.

ECG today: sinus rhythm 71, normal intervals, early repolarization only, no pre-excitation, Brugada or ARVC features.

Impression: Palpitations most consistent with sinus tachycardia related to anxiety and, earlier, stimulants. Exam and ECG argue against HCM or a channelopathy, but given an unexplained sudden death at 34 in a second-degree relative, a baseline evaluation is appropriate.

Recommendations:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram.
2. 48-hour Holter monitor with symptom diary, including a gym session.
3. May resume full training in the meantime; stop and seek care for exertional syncope or chest pain.
4. If both are normal, no further routine testing; consider screening ECG/echo for his sister as well.
I will contact him with results.

reports.text:
Indication: palpitations; family history of sudden death.
Left ventricle: normal size (LVIDd 5.0 cm) and wall thickness (IVSd 0.9 cm, PWd 0.9 cm). LVEF 62% by biplane Simpson. No regional wall motion abnormality. Normal diastolic function for age. No LVOT obstruction at rest or with Valsalva.
Right ventricle: normal size and systolic function (TAPSE 2.4 cm); no RV dilation or regional dyskinesia.
Atria: normal size.
Valves: structurally normal; trace physiologic tricuspid and pulmonic regurgitation. No mitral valve prolapse.
Coronary ostia: origins visualized from the appropriate sinuses.
Aorta: normal root 3.0 cm.
No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal collapse.
reports.conclusion: Structurally normal heart; LVEF 62%; no hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

reports.text:
Recording duration 47 h 52 min, analyzable 99%.
Predominant rhythm sinus. Heart rate min 51 bpm (sleep, 03:20), max 152 bpm (17:48, during patient-marked gym session), mean 76 bpm.
Supraventricular ectopy: 14 isolated PACs; no couplets, no runs of SVT, no atrial fibrillation.
Ventricular ectopy: 3 isolated PVCs, uniform. No couplets or VT.
No pauses > 2 seconds. No AV block.
Diary: 3 entries ('heart racing' at 07:55 work, 'nervous' 13:10, 'pounding' gym 17:45) correlate with sinus rhythm at 104, 98 and 148 bpm respectively.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with appropriate rate response; rare PACs and PVCs; symptoms correlate with sinus tachycardia.

documents.title: Results — Echo and Holter
documents.body:
Telephone with pt and Spanish interpreter. Reviewed: echo structurally normal, EF 62%, normal wall thickness, no LVOT obstruction. Holter 48 h: sinus rhythm 51-152, rare PACs/PVCs, all 3 diary events = sinus tachycardia.
Assessment: benign palpitations from sinus tachycardia; no evidence of cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia. No restrictions on work, gym or soccer. Avoid stimulants/pre-workout. Follow up with cardiology only for exertional syncope, chest pain or sustained palpitations. Suggested his younger sister have a baseline ECG through her pediatrician given the uncle's history. Letter copied to PCP.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily with food as needed for pain, up to 10 days

reports.text:
Right ankle, 3 views (AP, mortise, lateral).
Indication: inversion injury 2 days ago, lateral malleolar tenderness.
Findings: No acute fracture or dislocation. Ankle mortise is congruent with symmetric joint spaces. Talar dome intact. Moderate soft tissue swelling over the lateral malleolus. Base of the fifth metatarsal included on the lateral view and intact. No joint effusion of significance.
Impression: Lateral soft tissue swelling without fracture.
reports.conclusion: No fracture; lateral soft tissue swelling.

documents.title: Acute Visit — Right Ankle
documents.body:
Seen by covering NP. English with some Spanish; pt declined interpreter.

S: Sat 7/12 rolled R ankle inward stepping on another player's foot at pickup soccer. Heard no pop. Swelled within an hour, limped off. Iced, wrapped with an ACE from work, elevated. Can walk but limping, worse on stairs. Pain 6/10 lateral ankle. No numbness. No prior ankle injuries. Took 2 OTC ibuprofen twice yesterday. On sertraline 100 mg; no other meds.

O: Antalgic gait, bears weight 4+ steps. R ankle: moderate swelling and ecchymosis lateral, maximal tenderness over ATFL, also tender at posterior edge distal fibula. No medial malleolar, navicular or 5th MT base tenderness. Anterior drawer mildly lax with soft endpoint vs L. Squeeze test neg. Achilles intact (Thompson neg). DP/PT 2+, sensation intact.
X-ray (in-office, 3 views): no fracture; lateral soft tissue swelling.

A/P: R lateral ankle sprain, grade II (ATFL).
- Lace-up ankle brace; weight bear as tolerated; ice/elevate, compression first 72 h.
- Ibuprofen 600 mg TID with food up to 10 days. Small added bleeding risk with SSRI -- take with food, stop if dark stools or GI pain.
- PT for proprioception/strength -- pt works at a PT clinic and can be evaluated there; referral written.
- Modified duty note for work x1 wk (mostly on feet as aide).
- Return if unable to bear weight, numbness, or no improvement in 2 wks.
Recheck PRN; anxiety f/u with PCP as planned.

documents.title: Work Note — Modified Duty
documents.body: Pt called -- employer needs the restrictions in writing on letterhead before he can work tomorrow. Letter completed per NP's 7/14 plan: may work with R ankle brace; seated or light tasks preferred, no ladder use, no carrying loads > 20 lb, breaks to elevate as needed, 7/15-7/21; full duty thereafter if improving. No diagnosis disclosed on letter per pt request. Uploaded to portal and faxed to employer HR number provided by pt.

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up — Anxiety
documents.body:
Video, Spanish. Pt at home. F/u overdue -- planned after cardiology in June, rescheduled twice around his work schedule.

Interval: Cardiology work-up (echo, Holter) normal in June -- benign sinus tachycardia, no restrictions. Did 6 CBT sessions with BH (Apr-Aug); stopped in August when he enrolled in evening anatomy & physiology at the community college -- 'I have the tools now.' One mild panic attack in July in a crowded store, used breathing, passed in a few minutes. Back in the stockroom at work without problem. Worry 'mucho menos.' Sleeping ~7 h. No caffeine beyond 1 coffee.
Ankle: did 4 weeks of PT exercises at work, back to soccer with brace, no pain.
Sertraline 100 mg daily, no side effects, no missed doses. Denies SI.

GAD-7 6 (from 13 in March), PHQ-9 3.

A/P:
1. GAD with panic disorder -- much improved on sertraline 100 + CBT. Continue current dose at least through the school year; discuss taper only after 6-12 mo stable and a calm stretch, not before exams. OK to return to BH anytime.
2. R ankle sprain -- resolved.
3. Flu shot this fall (nurse visit). Annual physical in winter.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Immunizations
documents.body: MA: Pt here for flu shot. Afebrile 36.6. Screening questions neg; amoxicillin allergy noted, not relevant to vaccines. Pt also asked for COVID booster -- works hands-on with patients; reviewed current recommendation with RN, pt wants it. Influenza 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; COVID-19 mRNA 2025-26 IM R deltoid. VIS given (Spanish). Observed 15 min, no reaction. Pt left ambulatory.

documents.title: mole on my back
documents.body: Hi, one of the PTs at my job was showing me a scapula exercise and she said a mole on my upper back looks weird, kinda dark and uneven on one side and she said get it checked. I cant see it good but my mom took a picture, its like the size of a pencil eraser, brown with a darker part on the side. I think it was smaller before but im not sure. doesnt hurt or bleed. should I come in? thank you

documents.title: RE: mole on my back
documents.body:
Hola Josue, gracias por avisar -- your coworker gave good advice. A mole that is uneven in color or may be growing should be looked at in person. Front desk will call to book a 30-minute visit; if it looks atypical I can do a small shave biopsy the same day. Nothing to do before then. If it bleeds or changes quickly, let us know sooner.
-- PCP

reports.text:
Specimen: Skin, left upper back, paramedian, shave biopsy.
Gross: Received in formalin, a tan-brown shave of skin, 0.8 x 0.6 x 0.1 cm, with a variegated brown macule 0.7 x 0.5 cm. Inked, serially sectioned, entirely submitted.
Microscopic: Sections show a compound melanocytic proliferation with lentiginous and nested junctional growth, bridging of rete ridges and shouldering of the junctional component beyond the dermal component. Concentric and lamellar dermal fibroplasia. Melanocytes show mild cytologic atypia. Dermal component matures with descent. No dermal mitoses, no pagetoid spread, no ulceration.
Margins: The junctional component extends to a peripheral margin. Deep margin clear.
Diagnosis: Compound dysplastic (atypical) nevus with mild atypia, extending to a peripheral margin.
reports.conclusion: Compound dysplastic nevus, mild atypia; peripheral margin involved.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Skin Lesion — Shave Biopsy
documents.body:
Spanish.

S: Mole on L upper back noticed by coworker ~2 wks ago as darker/uneven; pt unsure if grown. No itch, bleeding. Sunburns a few times as a teen, no tanning beds. No personal or family hx of skin cancer that he knows of. Meds: sertraline 100 mg.

O: L upper back, 4 cm left of midline at T4 level: 7 x 5 mm macule, asymmetric, two shades of brown with darker eccentric area at the lateral edge, border slightly irregular, no elevation or ulceration. Rest of back: ~10 small uniform brown nevi < 4 mm. No palpable axillary nodes. No dermatoscope in office today.

Procedure: Shave (saucerization) biopsy. Verbal and written consent (Spanish form), risks incl. scar, infection, possible need for further removal. Site marked, prepped with chlorhexidine. 1% lidocaine w/ epi 1.5 mL. Deep shave with flexible blade to include visible pigment with ~1 mm rim. Hemostasis with aluminum chloride. Petrolatum + bandage. EBL minimal. Tolerated well. Specimen to pathology.

A/P: Atypical-appearing pigmented lesion, L upper back -- shave biopsy done. Wound care sheet given: keep covered, petrolatum daily, gentle washing, expect pink scar. Will call with path ~1 wk. Sunscreen SPF 30+ on outdoor soccer days.

conditions.label: Dysplastic nevus of trunk
conditions.note: Compound dysplastic nevus, mild atypia, peripheral margin involved

documents.title: Skin Biopsy Result
documents.body: Path (resulted 11/14): compound dysplastic nevus with mild atypia, peripheral margin involved, deep margin clear. Not melanoma. Called pt, discussed in Spanish: this is an 'atypical mole,' not cancer; mild atypia with a positive edge is often watched rather than re-cut, but since he has many nevi and the lesion looked atypical, referring to dermatology for a full skin exam and their opinion on re-excision. Biopsy site healing, no redness. Pt relieved, agrees.

documents.title: Dermatology Referral
documents.body: Dermatology referral placed: mildly dysplastic nevus L upper back, peripheral margin involved (path 11/14 attached); please advise on re-excision vs observation and do full-body skin exam. Spanish interpreter. Derm next new-patient opening 2/10/26 -- booked, pt notified by text, on cancellation list.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.body:
Annual preventive visit, in Spanish.

Interval since establishing 12/2024: ED 3/2025 panic attack; panic disorder dx, sertraline 50 -> 100 mg; 6 CBT sessions; cardiology 5/2025 with normal echo and 48-h Holter (sinus tach, rare PACs). R ankle sprain 7/2025, resolved. Shave biopsy L upper back 11/2025 -- mildly dysplastic nevus, margin involved; derm 2/10.

Today: feels well. Anxiety 'controlada.' No panic attacks since July. Fall semester A&P I -- got a B+; taking A&P II this spring and applying to a PTA program for fall 2026. Still full-time PT aide. Lifting 4x/wk, indoor soccer. No palpitations. Sleep 7 h. Diet: rice/beans/chicken at home, fast food 2-3x/wk at work. Alcohol 2-3 drinks/month, no binges. Never smoked, no vaping since 2023. No drugs. Not sexually active currently; condoms discussed. Seatbelt yes. No firearms at home.

Meds: sertraline 100 mg daily; cetirizine PRN spring. Allergy: amoxicillin (rash).
FHx: mother anxiety, hypothyroid; father HTN; MGM T2DM; maternal uncle sudden death at 34 (cardiology aware; sister had a normal ECG through her pediatrician per mother).

ROS negative except as above.
Exam: BMI 24.6. Well. Skin: biopsy site L upper back healed, flat pink 8 mm scar, no repigmentation. HEENT, neck, thyroid nl. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. GU deferred (pt declined, asymptomatic). MSK: R ankle stable, full ROM. Neuro nl. Mood good, affect bright.
PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 5, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance -- HIV/HCV screened 12/2024. Lipids nl 12/2024; no repeat. Immunizations: Tdap 2018 (due 2028), HPV complete (2 doses started <15), MenACWY booster 2023; MenB discussed (shared decision 16-23), declined. Flu + COVID done 10/2025. Sun protection.
2. GAD/panic disorder -- stable on sertraline 100. Continue; no taper during application season. BH open door.
3. Palpitations -- resolved; benign work-up. Remove from active list.
4. Dysplastic nevus -- derm 2/10.
RTC ~6 mo or PRN; will need PTA program health forms when accepted.

events.reason: Dysplastic nevus with involved margin; full skin exam

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, low MDM

documents.title: Dermatology New Patient
documents.body:
Referred by PCP for a mildly dysplastic nevus of the L upper back (shave 11/10/25, peripheral margin involved) and full skin exam. Interpreter by phone for parts of visit; pt mostly English.

Hx: No personal/family hx of melanoma. Occasional sunburns as a teen, plays soccer outdoors. Fitzpatrick III-IV. Meds: sertraline.

TBSE (scalp to feet incl. palms/soles, nails, oral mucosa): ~25 melanocytic nevi, mostly trunk, all < 5 mm, symmetric, uniform. Dermoscopy of 4 larger trunk nevi: reticular/globular benign patterns. Biopsy site L upper back: 9 mm flat pink-white scar, no pigment at edges on dermoscopy. No suspicious lesions elsewhere.

A/P:
1. Dysplastic nevus, mild atypia, peripheral margin involved -- per current consensus, mildly atypical nevi with positive margins and no residual clinical pigment can be observed; re-excision not needed. Monitor the scar: return if any pigment reappears.
2. Multiple benign nevi -- no biopsy today. Monthly self-checks (sister/mother to check back), photo comparison.
3. Sun protection: SPF 30+ broad spectrum, reapply on soccer days, hat.
Follow up in 12 months for skin exam, sooner for any changing lesion. Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: ansiedad / receta
documents.body: Doctora buenas noches. He estado muy ansioso estas semanas con el examen de anatomía y la entrevista del programa de PTA, casi no duermo. Tambien la farmacia dijo que la receta de sertralina estaba vencida y tardaron como 5 dias en arreglarlo, estuve sin tomarla y me sentía mareado y como corrientazos en la cabeza. Ya la empecé otra vez el sábado y estoy mejor del mareo. Tuve un ataque de pánico pequeño en la biblioteca. Puedo hablar con usted esta semana o la otra? gracias

documents.title: RE: ansiedad / receta
documents.body:
Hola Josue. Siento mucho lo de la farmacia. El mareo y los 'corrientazos' son síntomas de suspender la sertralina de golpe; no son peligrosos y deben quitarse en unos días ahora que la está tomando otra vez. Ya mandé una receta nueva por 90 días con refills para todo el año. Le pedí a recepción una cita por video el martes 4/21. Si se siente en peligro o con pensamientos de hacerse daño, llame al 988 (opción español).
[English summary: discontinuation symptoms after 5 missed doses explained; new 90-day sertraline 100 mg Rx with refills sent; video visit 4/21; 988 reviewed.]
-- PCP

Denies SI, no self-harm.

- Continue sertraline 100 mg; new 90-day Rx with refills sent 4/15. Discussed increase to 150 mg; he prefers to restart CBT first since it worked last year and the stress is time-limited. Agreed; revisit dose if GAD-7 not improving in 6-8 wks.

Spanish.

S: Accepted to the PTA program at the community college, starts in September -- very happy. Semester done. Restarted CBT with BH in May (3 sessions so far, telehealth). Sleeping 7 h with phone out of the bedroom. No panic attacks since April. Sertraline 100 mg daily, no missed doses since restarting, refills in place. Denies SI.
Program needs for clinical placements: physical exam form, hep B immunity, TB screen, immunization record, flu shot by October.

O: BP 118/74, HR 68, wt 74.9 kg. Well, relaxed. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Biopsy scar L upper back flat, no pigment.
GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 4.

A/P:
1. GAD/panic disorder -- improving after spring flare. Continue sertraline 100 mg + CBT. No change.
2. PTA program clearance -- hep B surface antibody and QuantiFERON today (born in DR, a moderate-incidence country; no other exposures; IGRA preferred given likely infant BCG). MMR x2, varicella x2, hep B x3 documented from DR card per pediatric records; Tdap 2018. Will complete form once labs back.
3. Dysplastic nevus -- stable scar; derm f/u 2/2027.

events.reason: Lab results — hepatitis B antibody, QuantiFERON

documents.title: Program Labs
documents.body: QuantiFERON negative -- no latent TB. Hep B surface antibody 4 mIU/mL (<10 = not protective). Common years after an infant series; he has a documented 3-dose series. Plan per CDC for health-care students: one booster dose now, recheck anti-HBs 1-2 months later; if still <10, complete a second series. RN called pt in Spanish, explained; nurse visit booked 7/7.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Hepatitis B Vaccine
documents.body: RN: Hep B booster (challenge dose) for PTA program, anti-HBs 4 on 6/16. Pt feels well, no fever, no yeast allergy. Engerix-B 20 mcg/1 mL IM R deltoid. VIS (Spanish) given. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Lab order placed for anti-HBs after 8/11; pt to come on a day off work. Reminder set.

documents.title: Hepatitis B Antibody — Post-Booster
documents.body: Anti-HBs 186 mIU/mL after booster 7/7 (was 4). Immune; no further hep B doses or titers needed. Portal message to pt: 'Ya está protegido contra hepatitis B.' Will complete program form.

documents.title: Program Health Form Completed
documents.body: Clinical-placement health form for PTA program completed by PCP and signed: exam 1/20/26 and 6/16/26, no restrictions. Immunizations: Tdap 9/2018; MMR x2 and varicella x2 (DR card, transcribed 2018); hep B x3 + booster 7/7/26, anti-HBs 186 on 8/18/26; influenza 10/2025 (2026-27 dose to be sent when given). TB: QuantiFERON negative 6/16/26. Pt picked up original at front desk; copy scanned and uploaded to portal. Pt reminded flu shot due before October clinical start.
